credits.creator: Sandy Kurt
credits.note: The construction follows her nineteen steps, and the lines inked are those of her finished drawing; the step text is our own.

given.A: Any point to the right of O. The distance OA is the radius of the main circle, and the unit for every length.

steps.text: Draw a circle around the centre. Its radius is the unit for the whole pattern.
Draw the horizontal through the centre and the vertical at right angles to it. They cut the circle at four points.
Halve each right angle to get the two diagonals. The circle is now divided into eight.
Draw the two squares inside the circle: one standing on its corners at the ends of the horizontal and vertical, one lying flat with its corners on the diagonals. They cross at eight points.
Rule a line through the centre and each crossing of the squares. With the first lines, the circle is divided into sixteen.

Put the compass on the crossing just above the horizontal on the right and open it until the circle just touches the horizontal and the diagonal. Keep that opening and draw the same circle on the other seven crossings and on the centre.
Join the centres of the ring circles with two horizontal and two vertical lines, then with four diagonal lines. Each line runs through two centres.
Where the upper horizontal line crosses the steep line through the centre, put the compass and draw the circle that just touches the vertical and the diagonal.
Put the compass on the centre and draw the circle that just touches that small circle on its near side. With the same opening, draw a circle around each of the eight crossings of the squares.

Where two of the diagonal lines cross on the horizontal, draw the circle that just touches the ring circles around it. Draw the same circle at the seven other places where two of the joining lines cross on the vertical or the diagonals.
Join every ring-circle centre to the centre two places round. The eight lines make two more squares, turned a sixteenth of a turn from the first two.
Mark where the circles around the crossings of the squares cut the new lines, and through those points rule vertical lines, in pairs.
Mark where the circles around the crossings of the squares cut the new lines, and through those points rule horizontal lines, in pairs.
Mark where the circles around the crossings of the squares cut the new lines, and through those points rule slanting up to the left lines, in pairs.
Mark where the circles around the crossings of the squares cut the new lines, and through those points rule slanting up to the right lines, in pairs.

Draw an octagon inside each ring circle, each small circle and the centre circle, with its corners where the circle meets lines through its centre parallel to the horizontal, the vertical and the diagonals.
For the star in the middle, mark where the circle around the centre crosses the sixteen lines through the centre, and join the marks three places apart with lines in pairs.

Draw the square that just touches the main circle: a line at right angles to the horizontal at each side, and at right angles to the vertical at the top and bottom. This square is the tile that repeats.
Mark the crossings where the pattern turns.

Now set the rows: each row sits half a wheel along from the one below, as close as the wheels allow. Put the compass on the centre of the small circle above the middle and draw the circle through the middle; where it crosses the vertical again is the bottom of the next row. Rule the horizontal there, and through the bottom-right corner of the square rule a line parallel to the line from the bottom-left corner to that mark. The slanted box between them is the tile.

ink.text: Go over the lines of the finished wheel: the octagons, the bands between them and the star in the middle.

pattern.text: Repeat the slanted tile edge to edge. Each row of wheels sits half a wheel along from the row below and as close as it can come, the large octagons of neighbouring rows meeting corner to corner.

expect.note: Golden values in units of OA. Rows half a wheel apart sideways and 2√2 − 1 apart upward (the owner's suggestion, as close as the wheels allow); the kites and the joint star are small by design.
